text:
You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.75 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where each token contributed returns 3x total split among all members, so the group optimum is full contribution while the individually dominant strategy is to contribute nothing. Since it repeats over 10 rounds, I'll open with a moderately cooperative contribution, maybe around 10, to signal good faith.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where each token contributed returns 0.75 to every member, making full contribution socially optimal even though keeping tokens is individually dominant. Since it's a 10-round repeated game, opening with cooperation could encourage reciprocity from others, so I'll contribute the full 20.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a classic public goods game: each contributed token returns 3x total but only 0.75 to the contributor, so self-interest favors free-riding even though full cooperation yields a better payoff for everyone. With 10 repeated rounds, there's tension between the dominant strategy of contributing nothing and the cooperative outcome of everyone contributing fully.

I'll start by contributing 20 to signal cooperative intent, then adjust in later rounds based on how others respond.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking: This is a public goods game where each token contributed returns 3 total to the group but only 0.75 to me, so keeping tokens is individually dominant even though full contribution maximizes group welfare. Still, leaning toward cooperation seems like the better choice here, so I'll lean toward contributing a meaningful amount.

calls.text: Round 2 of 10. Last round you put 10 tokens in the group account, it received 70 in total, and you got 62.5 points.

reply.thinking:
Let me verify: with group total 70, the other three members contributed 60 total, averaging 20 each—that's quite cooperative. My payoff comes to 10 (kept) plus 52.5 (share of group) for 62.5, which checks out. Since others are contributing heavily, I'm weighing whether to raise my own contribution too, though keeping a token still nets me more individually than contributing it.

Pure self-interest says contribute zero, but sustaining cooperation argues for giving more. I'll settle on contributing 15—enough to signal reciprocity without fully exposing myself to exploitation.

calls.text: Round 2 of 10. Last round you put 20 tokens in the group account, it received 70 in total, and you got 52.5 points.

reply.thinking: The group pot totals 70, so the other three members contributed 50 between them, matching my 52.5 payout from 75% of the pool. Since others averaged around 16.7 in contributions, I'll keep cooperating for now and contribute 20 again to see how the group responds.

reply.thinking: Round 1 confirmed: I contributed 20, others contributed 50 total, earning me 52.5. For round 2, I'll stick with full cooperation at 20 to help sustain group contributions.

calls.text: Round 3 of 10. Last round you put 15 tokens in the group account, it received 75 in total, and you got 61.25 points.

reply.thinking:
Checking the math: with group size 75, others contributed 60 total, so my payoff comes to 5 + 75*0.75 = 61.25. Others seem to hold steady around 20 average contribution each—I'm wondering if there's room to exploit this by keeping more tokens, since contributing costs me 1 but only returns 0.75 to me personally.

That means every token I keep nets me an extra 0.25 compared to contributing, so dropping to 10 could gain 1.25 per round, but that risks triggering retaliation if others notice. I'll stick with 15 to keep things stable rather than testing the group's patience.
